teas.description_brief: Lightly oxidized oolong from Taiwan's Alishan mountain range, grown above 1000m. Known for intense floral fragrance and creamy texture.
A unique green tea (not white, despite the name) from Anji county known for its pale color and high amino acid content. The albino cultivar produces exceptionally umami-rich tea.
The highest grade of white tea, made exclusively from unopened buds covered in silvery-white down. Subtle sweetness with notes of melon, hay, and honey.
White tea featuring one bud and two leaves, offering more body and complexity than Silver Needle at a more accessible price.
Prized spring green tea from Dongting Mountain near Tai Lake, known for its tightly curled spiral shape resembling snail shells. Grown among fruit trees, it absorbs natural fruity sweetness.
Prized sheng pu'er from Bingdao village. Intensely sweet, cooling, and floral with a thick body and long finish.
The king of Wuyi rock oolongs, legendary for the original mother trees that produced tea worth more than gold. Deep mineral character from the rocky terroir.
One of Taiwan's highest elevation oolongs, grown above 2,000m. Exceptionally clean, floral, and sweet with a cooling finish.
Yunnan black tea made entirely of golden buds. Rich, malty, and honey-sweet with a thick, velvety body.
Traditional Taiwanese oolong with medium roast, offering balance between floral freshness and toasty warmth. One of Taiwan's original famous teas.
Biluochun, literally "green snail spring," is one of China's ten famous teas, grown among fruit trees on Dongting Mountain. Its tiny, curled leaves yield a delicate, sweet, and floral liquor.
Premium green tea from the misty peaks of Huangshan (Yellow Mountain) in Anhui province. Named for its downy white tips, it produces a delicate orchid-like fragrance.
Hand-rolled green tea pearls scented with fresh jasmine blossoms over multiple nights. Watch the pearls unfurl to release intense floral fragrance.
Hand-rolled jasmine tea pearls that unfurl as they steep. Intensely fragrant, sweet, and soothing with a clean finish.
Premium black tea from Wuyi made entirely from golden buds. Created in 2005, it quickly became one of China's most sought-after teas.
Old-tree tea from Jingmai Mountain. Floral and honeyed with a distinctive orchid aroma and lingering sweetness.
The most famous yellow tea, made only on Junshan Island in Dongting Lake. The unique 'sealed yellowing' process creates a mellower flavor than green tea.
The 'Burgundy of teas,' Keemun is prized for its wine-like aroma and smooth, complex flavor. Created in 1875, it became a key component of English Breakfast.
Premium grade Keemun made from tender buds. Wine-like, fruity, and floral with the signature Keemun sweetness and little astringency.
Classic Keemun black tea. Fruity, floral, and wine-like with the signature Keemun sweetness.
Ripe pu'er from Lao Banzhang village. Thick, earthy, and powerful with a sweet, lasting finish.
The 'King of Pu'er' from Lao Banzhang village. Known for its powerful, bitter-sweet character that transforms into intense returning sweetness (huigan).
Unique green tea made only from single leaves (no buds or stems), shaped like melon seeds. One of China's historic famous teas from Anhui province.
Dark tea from Guangxi province with distinctive betel nut aroma. Ages beautifully and traditionally valued for digestive properties.

Famous Anhui green tea whose name means "Lu'an Melon Seed" for its flat, oval, seed-like leaves. Unique among Chinese greens for being made without buds or stems, yielding a sweet, orchid-laden cup with a silky texture.
Classic raw pu'er recipe from Menghai Tea Factory. Balanced, slightly bitter, and excellent for aging with notes of apricot and camphor.
Classic ripe pu'er recipe from Menghai Tea Factory. Smooth, earthy, and reliable with notes of dark cocoa and wet forest.
Ripe pu'er from the renowned Menghai region, processed using accelerated fermentation. Smooth, earthy complexity with notes of forest floor, dates, and dark chocolate.
Honey-orchid fragrance dancong from Phoenix Mountain. Intensely aromatic with honeyed fruit and orchid notes.
Single-bush oolongs from Phoenix Mountain, each tree producing unique aromatic profiles. Mi Lan Xiang (Honey Orchid) is the most famous variety.
Popular Wuyi rock oolong known for its distinctive cinnamon-like aroma and spicy character. Often blended with Shui Xian.
High mountain oolong from Shan Lin Xi, Taiwan. Grown around 1,500m, it is floral, creamy, and remarkably smooth with little astringency.
Premium Longjing from Lion Peak, the most prized sub-region of West Lake Hangzhou. Prized for its jade color, flat leaves, and pronounced chestnut sweetness.
Ancient Wuyi cultivar producing smooth, orchid-scented rock oolong. Often aged, developing deeper complexity over time.
Distinctive green tea with exceptionally large, flat leaves pressed during processing. One of China's Top Ten Famous Teas, prized for its elegant orchid fragrance.
China's most popular oolong, named after the Buddhist bodhisattva Guanyin. Intense orchid fragrance and creamy texture with a sweet finish.
The iconic Anxi oolong named after the Iron Goddess of Mercy. Ranges from fresh floral to deeply roasted; classic versions balance orchid aroma with a creamy body.

China's most famous green tea, prized for its flat, smooth leaves and distinctive chestnut flavor. Authentic Xi Hu Longjing comes only from the West Lake area of Hangzhou and is hand-pan-fired to halt oxidation.
Duck-Shit Fragrance dancong, now one of the most sought-after Phoenix oolongs. Creamy, floral, and intensely aromatic with a long finish.
Old-tree sheng pu'er from Yiwu. Elegant, floral, and honey-sweet with a soft, silky texture and long aftertaste.
Raw pu'er from the historic Yiwu tea region, known for producing elegant, aromatic sheng that ages gracefully with honey sweetness and floral notes.
Robust black tea from Yunnan made with large-leaf varietals, displaying abundant golden tips. Bold malty sweetness, honeyed character, and no astringency.
The original black tea, created in the Wuyi Mountains during the Ming Dynasty. Traditional versions are pine-smoked, while modern styles focus on natural longan-like sweetness.
White tea aged for several years, developing complex herbal and medicinal notes. Traditionally valued in Fujian for its health properties.
Heicha from Anhua in Hunan province. Earthy, sweet, and smooth with notes of dried jujube and aged wood.
One of the Four Famous Wuyi Rock Teas, named for its pale yellow-green leaves. Lighter than most yancha with delicate, honey-sweet character.
Traditional Fujian black tea from Bailin. Delicate, floral, and slightly sweet with a reddish-gold liquor.
Traditional Anxi oolong cultivar often compared to Tie Guan Yin. Smooth, floral, and slightly less aromatic than its famous cousin.
Wuyi yancha named after the late-arriving spring. Light, floral, and mineral with a refreshing character.
Raw pu'er from Bulang Mountain, known for powerful, bitter character similar to Lao Banzhang but more accessible. Ages well.
White tea from Cangling in Zhejiang. Delicate, floral, and refreshingly sweet with a pale golden liquor.
Ripe pu'er blended with chrysanthemum flowers. Earthy, cooling, and soothing with a gentle floral lift.
Eyebrow-shaped green tea, primarily produced for export. Offers good value with a plummy, slightly tart character.
Large-leaf Anxi oolong with a full, smooth body and a long-lasting floral aroma.
Flat-pressed green tea from Anhui with a roasted chestnut character similar to Longjing but with a fuller body and longer finish.
Fine green tea from Guizhou province, known for its delicate appearance and sweet, chestnut flavor. Growing recognition in recent years.
One of the few remaining Chinese steamed green teas, similar to Japanese processing. Produces a vivid green liquor with strong umami character.
Hunan dark tea famous for its golden flower fungus (Eurotium cristatum) that develops during processing, contributing to its unique flavor and health properties.
Leafy white tea from Fuding with a robust, sweet, and slightly earthy character. Excellent for aging.
Fujian silver-needle style green tea with fuzzy white buds. Delicate, sweet, and floral with very little astringency.
Medium-grade Anhua dark tea with a robust, earthy profile and a mellow sweet aftertaste.
White tea made from larger leaves and fewer buds than Shou Mei. Earthy, sweet, and commonly aged for deeper flavor.
Grade between White Peony and Shou Mei, using slightly finer leaves. Good balance of affordability and quality.
Fine green tea from Suichuan in Jiangxi. Tiny twisted leaves produce a bright, brisk, and sweet infusion.
Oolong tea scented with sweet osmanthus flowers. The natural apricot-like sweetness of osmanthus pairs beautifully with oolong's complexity.
Tightly rolled green tea pellets, traditionally for export. The leaves slowly unfurl during brewing, releasing bold, slightly smoky flavor.
Purple bamboo shoot green tea from Guzhu. Tender purple-tinged buds with a sweet, floral, and refreshing character.
Anxi oolong known for its natural osmanthus-like fragrance. Earlier harvest than Tie Guan Yin, with a lighter, more floral character.
Yellow Branch Fragrance dancong with bright floral and citrus notes. Elegant and complex with a clean finish.
Fragrant Anxi oolong known as Golden Osmanthus. Light oxidation gives it a bright floral aroma with a sweet, silky liquor.
Green brick tea from Hubei, traditionally compressed for transport. Mellow, earthy, and slightly sweet.
Robust black tea from Hunan. Bold, sweet, and slightly smoky with a thick, warming body.
Yellow tea from Huoshan in Anhui province. More accessible than Junshan Yinzhen while offering similar mellow, sweet character.
White tea Silver Needle base scented with jasmine. Combines the delicacy of white tea with the fragrance of jasmine.
Delicate jasmine-scented white tea buds. Light, floral, and naturally sweet with a creamy mouthfeel.
High-grade jasmine tea using silver-tip green tea base. Light and refreshing with balanced floral character.
High-mountain green tea from Jinggangshan. Tender buds yield a bright, grassy infusion with a clean sweet finish.
Green tea from Jingshan with a long monastic history. Delicate, sweet, and mildly nutty with a clean finish.
Rare black tea from the Longjing region of Hangzhou. Delicate and nuanced with plum-like sweetness and floral notes.
Award-winning green tea from Kaihua County in Zhejiang. Known for its sharp, pine-needle shape, bright green color, and fresh vegetal flavor.
Traditional Tibetan border tea brick. Robust, earthy, and slightly smoky with a thick body.
Keemun made in a green-tea style with twisted leaves. Bright, floral, and slightly lighter than standard Keemun.
Ripe pu'er from Lincang prefecture, home to ancient tea trees. Known for clean, sweet character with less earthiness than Menghai.
From Taiwan's highest elevation tea gardens (1800-2500m). Exceptionally refined with delicate pear and orchid notes.
Green tea from the misty slopes of Mount Lushan in Jiangxi. The high humidity and cloud cover produce tender leaves with delicate flavor.
Anxi oolong known as Hairy Crab. Light, floral, and slightly creamy with a brisk finish.
Longjing from the Meijiawu village, one of the five core Longjing production areas. Slightly more affordable than Xi Hu proper but excellent quality.
Historic green tea from Mengding Mountain in Sichuan, claimed birthplace of cultivated tea. Sweet, mellow character with good complexity.
Yellow tea from Mengding Mountain in Sichuan, claimed birthplace of cultivated tea. Sweet, mellow character with good complexity.
Classic raw pu'er recipe with larger leaves. Balanced, slightly astringent, and excellent for aging.
Representative raw pu'er from Menghai. Floral, bitter-sweet, and evolving with age.
Traditional heavily roasted Taiwanese style Tie Guan Yin from the Muzha district. Rich, complex with dried fruit and caramel notes.
Sheng pu'er from Nannuo Mountain, home to the 'King of Tea Trees.' Known for balanced, approachable character with honey and floral notes.
Baozhong-style oolong from Nantou, Taiwan. Light, floral, and silky with a lingering aroma.
Ripe pu'er with sticky rice fragrance. Sweet, earthy, and comforting with a distinctive aromatic note.
Heavily oxidized Taiwanese oolong with characteristic honey and muscatel notes. The leaves must be bitten by leafhoppers, which triggers the unique flavor compounds.
Oolong scented with osmanthus flowers. The toasty oolong base is lifted by sweet, fruity osmanthus fragrance.
Rare Orchid Fragrance dancong. Elegant, floral, and complex with a long, sweet finish.
Thousand Tael Tea - a massive column of compressed Anhua dark tea. Aged, woody, and sweet with a deep reddish-brown liquor.
Yunnan black tea blended with dried rose petals. The rose adds floral sweetness that complements the honey notes of Dianhong.
Taiwanese red oolong from Sun Moon Lake. Honeyed, cinnamon-spiced, and full-bodied with a malty depth.
Made from mature white tea leaves, offering more body than Silver Needle or White Peony. Ages exceptionally well, developing rich, sweet complexity.
Golden Turtle Wuyi yancha. Smooth, mineral, and floral with a sweet, lasting aftertaste.
One of the Four Famous Wuyi Rock Teas. Named for a legendary dispute over the tea trees. Distinctive plum-like sweetness.
Aged Wuyi Shui Xian with deep woody, mineral, and orchid notes. Smooth and resonant with excellent depth.
Border tea historically traded to Tibet. Robust, earthy, and slightly smoky with a thick, warming body.
Black tea from Sichuan with distinctive citrus notes. A regional specialty with growing recognition.
Sichuan red tea made from tender buds. Sweet, mellow, and slightly fruity with a clean finish.
One of China's oldest named green teas, from Xiuning in Anhui. Tightly rolled pellets with a brisk, slightly astringent, and refreshing profile.
White Peony from Taimu Mountain in Fuding. Floral, fruity, and honeyed with a fuller body than Silver Needle.
Historic Fujian black tea from Tanyang. Smooth and sweet with a gentle fruity aroma and a clean finish.
One of the three Fujian gongfu black teas. Prized for its floral aroma and sweet, smooth character.
High-grade Anhua dark tea made from tender buds. Sweet, smooth, and complex with notes of dried fruit.
Green tea from Mount Tianmu with plump jade buds. Fresh, nutty, and slightly sweet with a silky mouthfeel.
One of the Four Famous Wuyi Rock Teas (Si Da Ming Cong). Named after an iron Buddhist statue, known for its robust, medicinal character.
Yellow tea from Weishan in Hunan. Plump buds yield a rich, sweet, and mellow liquor with a subtle roast.
Lightly oxidized twisted-leaf oolong from northern Taiwan. Fresh, floral, and silky with a lingering orchid aroma.
Curved eyebrow-shaped green tea from Wuyuan. Fresh, vegetal, and mildly nutty with a sweet finish.
Sheng pu'er from Xigui in Lincang. Bold, fragrant, and slightly astringent with a powerful sweet aftertaste.
Famous green tea from Henan province, known for its fine, needle-like leaves and fresh, vegetal flavor. One of China's Top Ten Famous Teas.
Despite its crude name (chosen to deter thieves), this dancong offers beautiful gardenia and almond notes. One of the most popular dancong varieties.
Silver Eyebrow black tea made from bud-and-leaf sets. Similar to Jin Jun Mei but more affordable, with a sweet, fruity character.
Black tea from Guangdong province, developed in the 1950s. Known for its strong, malty character and excellent value.
Robust black tea from Yingde in Guangdong. Bold, malty, and excellent with milk or as a breakfast tea.
Moonlight White from Yunnan, made from large-leaf cultivars. Sweet, fruity, and remarkably smooth with a distinctive two-tone leaf appearance.
Yunnan white tea with distinctive two-toned leaves (white on one side, dark on the other). Richer and more robust than Fujian white teas.
Sun-dried green tea from Yunnan made from large-leaf cultivars. Fuller and sweeter than eastern greens with a noticeable malt backbone.
Golden-bud Yunnan black tea with a mellow, sweet profile and notes of dried fruit and cocoa.
Compressed square cakes of Fujian Shuixian oolong. Floral, creamy, and smooth with a distinctive pressed shape.
Traditional Fujian black tea from Zhenghe. Smooth, sweet, and slightly floral with a reddish liquor.
Silver Needle from Zhenghe county, the other major white tea origin. Slightly grassier and more vegetal than Fuding style.
A classic dancong variety prized for its pure orchid fragrance. Lighter than Mi Lan Xiang with more delicate floral notes.
Premium green tea from Mount Emei in Sichuan. The flat, bamboo-leaf shaped leaves produce a refreshing, grassy infusion.
Green tea scented with lotus flowers. Fresh, floral, and delicately sweet with a clean finish.
Oolong scented with magnolia flowers. Creamy, floral, and elegant with a lingering fragrance.
Local green tea from the water-town region of Wuzhen. Light, refreshing, and mildly floral.
